newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli gunman says he aimed to save Hebron.
newsitem.headline: Israeli gunman says he aimed to save Hebron.

text.p: An Israeli soldier defended his shooting of seven Palestinian shoppers, insisting in a military court on Thursday: "All I did was fight for the liberation of the holy city of Hebron."
The gunman, 22-year-old soldier Noam Friedman, spoke to Israel Radio before a hearing in a court in Jaffa. The court ordered he be held another 10 days while charges are drawn up.

Last week Friedman fired his M-16 automatic rifle into the Arab market in Hebron, a West Bank town holy to Moslems and Jews as the burial place of the biblical Abraham. He said later he meant to kill as many Arabs as possible.

Friedman, an off-duty soldier from a settlement near Jerusalem, was wrestled to the ground by other Israeli soldiers. He said he wanted to sabotage the pending handover of most of the town to Palestinian self-rule.
An army prosecutor said the military was drawing up an indictment charging Friedman with attempted murder and causing harm in aggravated circumstances.

Friedman said this week the attack was also intended to avenge the death of Baruch Goldstein, a Jewish settler who massacred 29 Palestinian worshippers in a Hebron mosque in 1994. Goldstein was beaten to death by survivors.
Israel and the PLO say they are close to wrapping up a deal under which Israel would pull its troops out of 80 percent of Hebron, home to 400 Jews and 100,000 Arabs.
